properties.natural_language: Any inclusion list submitted by an external IL submitter must be validated against the current slot's committee assignment before being accepted into the local IL pool.
The IL submitter's validator index must be a member of the inclusion list committee for the current slot, as determined by get_inclusion_list_committee.
An inclusion list must reference a valid parent block hash that exists in the local fork choice store before it can be considered for inclusion.
After a valid inclusion list is accepted into the IL pool, it must be retrievable by (slot, validator_index) and its transactions are frozen for the remainder of the slot.
The inclusion list committee size is bounded by MAX_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE_SIZE and the committee composition is deterministic given the same beacon state and slot.

A block producer must include transactions satisfying the inclusion list before the block can pass fork choice validation; EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER input is untrusted and must be verified against the aggregated IL.
Before checking IL compliance, the block's execution payload must be fully decoded and the transaction list must be extractable without error.
After IL compliance check passes, the block is eligible for fork choice consideration. If it fails, the block must be rejected and not influence the canonical chain.
A block that does not satisfy the aggregated inclusion list for its slot must never become the head of the canonical chain.
The IL aggregation from multiple committee members is idempotent: aggregating the same set of ILs in any order yields the same satisfiability set of transactions.
After consensus on a slot completes, all inclusion lists for that slot are consumed and removed from the IL pool, preventing replay in future slots.
Each validator may submit at most one inclusion list per slot. Duplicate submissions from the same validator for the same slot must be rejected.

The FOCIL mechanism preserves liveness: if fewer than the threshold of committee members submit ILs, the block producer is not required to satisfy any inclusion constraint, but must still produce a valid block.
Before executing any JUMP or JUMPI instruction, the runtime must validate the destination against the set of valid JUMPDEST positions determined during code analysis.
An external contract deployer's bytecode must pass EOF validation (if EOF-prefixed) or legacy validation before being stored; untrusted EDGE-DEPLOY-REQUEST input must be fully validated.
An external message call's target address, calldata, and value must be validated against the current execution context's permissions before execution proceeds.
After a JUMP to a valid JUMPDEST, the program counter must be set to exactly that JUMPDEST position and execution resumes at the instruction immediately following the JUMPDEST byte.
After an invalid JUMP destination is detected, execution must immediately revert with an invalid jump destination error, consuming all remaining gas in the current call frame.
The JUMPDEST analysis table is immutable after initial code analysis: no execution path can add or remove valid jump destinations at runtime.
PUSH instruction data bytes are never valid JUMPDEST targets, even if the data byte equals 0x5B (the JUMPDEST opcode). The code analysis must correctly identify instruction boundaries.
After execution context initialization, the call stack depth is incremented by exactly 1 and must not exceed the maximum call depth of 1024.
The call stack depth never exceeds 1024. Any CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL, or CREATE at depth 1024 must fail without executing the target code.
After any EVM error (out of gas, stack overflow, invalid opcode), the current call frame must revert all state changes and return control to the parent frame with a failure indicator.
The program counter always points to a valid position within the code bounds (0 <= PC < len(code)). Execution at PC == len(code) results in a STOP.
The EVM stack size is bounded: it must contain at most 1024 elements. Any PUSH or DUP that would exceed this limit must trigger a stack overflow error.
Before executing any opcode, the stack must contain at least the number of elements required by that opcode's input specification.
A linter rule proposal must include a valid rule specification, target scope, and proposer identity before it can enter the governance review pipeline.
Linter governance rules are append-only: once a rule is ratified through governance, it cannot be silently removed; it can only be deprecated through another governance action.
The governance quorum threshold must be met before any rule state transition (proposal to ratified) is finalized. A quorum of zero is invalid.
After a linter rule is activated, all subsequent contract deployments in scope must be checked against the rule, and violations must be reported.
An EOF container submitted by an untrusted deployer must begin with the magic bytes 0xEF00 and contain a valid EOF version byte before any further structural validation proceeds.
The EOF container header must declare valid section sizes (type, code, container, data) that are consistent with the actual container length. Any mismatch must reject the container.
Each code section in an EOF container must have a corresponding type section entry specifying inputs, outputs, and max_stack_height. Missing type entries must cause validation failure.
After successful EOF container validation, the container is stored with its EOF prefix intact. The stored bytecode is byte-identical to the validated input.
After EOF execution initialization via EOFCREATE, the init container is executed in a new context and the returned bytes become the deployed code, which must itself be a valid EOF container.
EOF containers are immutable after deployment: no self-modifying code operations (CODECOPY, EXTCODECOPY into code section) are permitted within EOF execution context.
Legacy bytecode (non-EOF) cannot invoke EOF-specific opcodes (EOFCREATE, RETURNCONTRACT, CALLF, RETF, JUMPF). These opcodes must be undefined in legacy context.
EOF code cannot call legacy code via CREATE or CREATE2. EOF code must use EOFCREATE exclusively for contract creation.
The max_stack_height declared in the type section must equal the actual maximum stack height reached during abstract stack analysis of the code section. A mismatch must reject the container.
After a CALLF instruction, the return stack must contain the caller's code section index and PC, and execution resumes at that point upon RETF.
The return stack depth for EOF function calls must not exceed 1024. CALLF at depth 1024 must trigger an error.
After validation failure at any step, the EOF container is rejected entirely. Partial validation does not result in partial deployment.
An EOF container's data section size must be at least as large as the size declared in the header. Containers with truncated data sections are invalid except during EOFCREATE init execution.
A sync committee message received from an external P2P peer must be validated against the current sync committee membership and the peer's claimed validator index.
The sync committee message's beacon_block_root must reference a known block in the local store, and the message's slot must be within an acceptable range of the current slot.
A sync committee contribution received from a P2P peer must have a valid aggregation_bits field with at least one bit set and a valid BLS signature over the expected signing root.
Before accepting a contribution, the validator's subcommittee_index must be within [0, SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT) and the contribution must reference a known beacon_block_root.

After a valid sync committee message is accepted, it must be stored indexed by (slot, subcommittee_index, validator_index) and must not be replaced by a subsequent message from the same validator for the same slot.
During a fork transition to Altair, the sync committee is initialized from the beacon state at the fork boundary epoch. The committee composition is deterministic and must match across all nodes.
Each validator in the sync committee submits at most one message per slot. Duplicate messages from the same validator in the same slot must be ignored on gossip.
The message ID for sync committee gossip topics must be derived deterministically from the message content and the fork digest, preventing cross-fork message confusion.

After aggregating sync committee contributions into a SyncAggregate, the resulting aggregate must have sync_committee_bits reflecting exactly the participating validators and a valid aggregate signature.
Gossip messages on sync_committee_{subnet_id} topics must only contain messages from validators assigned to that specific subnet. Cross-subnet messages must be rejected.
Before executing KECCAK256, the memory offset and size must be validated: offset + size must not overflow uint256, and the memory expansion cost must be affordable with remaining gas.
The gas cost for KECCAK256 must be computed as 30 + 6 * ceil(size / 32) plus any memory expansion cost, and this total must not exceed available gas.
After KECCAK256 execution, exactly one 32-byte hash value is pushed onto the stack, the memory is unchanged, and gas is decremented by the computed cost.
KECCAK256 is a pure function: identical memory contents at any offset always produce the same hash. The result is independent of execution context, gas, or caller.
KECCAK256 of a zero-length input (size = 0) must return the well-known empty hash constant (0xc5d2...b3b7) regardless of the offset value.
After memory expansion for KECCAK256, the new memory size is max(old_size, offset + size) rounded up to the next 32-byte word. Memory beyond the old size is zero-initialized.
Memory expansion costs grow quadratically with size. The gas cost model ensures that very large memory allocations are prohibitively expensive, providing implicit DoS protection.
The stack must contain at least 2 elements (offset and size) before KECCAK256 execution. Stack underflow must trigger an immediate error.
An attestation received via gossip from an external validator must be validated: the committee index must be within bounds and the attestation data must reference a valid target epoch.
Under EIP-7549, the committee_index is moved out of AttestationData and into the Attestation container. Attestation validation must read committee_index from the new location.

Before aggregating attestations, all attestations in the aggregation set must share identical AttestationData (same source, target, beacon_block_root) and differ only in committee_index and aggregation_bits.

After aggregation under EIP-7549, the resulting aggregate attestation's committee_bits field must have exactly one bit set per participating committee, and the aggregation_bits must be the bitwise OR of all individual attestations per committee.
During fork transition to EIP-7549, attestations created pre-fork use the old format (committee_index in AttestationData) and post-fork use the new format. No mixed-format attestations are valid.
The maximum number of attestations per block is bounded. EIP-7549 changes the packing strategy but must not allow more aggregate attestations than MAX_ATTESTATIONS.
After gossip mutation under EIP-7549, the on_wire committee_bits encoding is transformed to the on_chain representation. The transformation must be lossless and reversible for signature verification.
Block size with EIP-7549 aggregate attestations must not exceed the maximum block size. The new committee_bits field is bounded by the number of committees per slot.
Attestation aggregation is commutative and associative: the order in which individual attestations are aggregated does not affect the final aggregate result.
A wallet_addEthereumChain request from an untrusted dApp must contain a valid chainId (hex-encoded, non-zero), at least one rpcUrls entry, and a nativeCurrency object with name, symbol, and decimals.
The chainId parameter must be a valid 0x-prefixed hex string representing a positive integer. Leading zeros beyond the 0x prefix must be rejected.
If the requested chainId already exists in the wallet, the method must switch to that chain (like wallet_switchEthereumChain) rather than adding a duplicate entry.
After successful chain addition, the new chain is persisted in the wallet's chain registry and can be selected for future transactions. The wallet must emit a chainChanged event.
The wallet must require explicit user approval before adding any new chain. Programmatic chain addition without user consent must never succeed, regardless of the dApp's origin.
RPC URLs provided in wallet_addEthereumChain must use HTTPS. Non-HTTPS URLs (except localhost for development) must be rejected to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on chain data.
The wallet must validate that the RPC endpoint actually serves the claimed chainId by querying eth_chainId. A mismatch between the declared and actual chainId must cause rejection.
After user rejection, the method must return error code 4001 (User Rejected Request) and no chain state changes occur in the wallet.
After validation failure (invalid params, invalid chainId format), the method must return error code -32602 (Invalid params) with a descriptive message.
The nativeCurrency.decimals must be a non-negative integer not exceeding 36. The symbol must be a non-empty string. These constraints prevent UI rendering issues and overflow.
Block explorer URLs, if provided, must be valid HTTPS URLs. The wallet must not auto-navigate to these URLs without user action to prevent phishing.
After the wallet switches to a newly added chain, the provider's chainId property must reflect the new chain and subsequent eth_call requests must route to the new chain's RPC.
The security boundary between dApp and wallet must prevent the dApp from reading the wallet's existing chain list, private keys, or account balances through the wallet_addEthereumChain method.
Before initiating an EVM trace, the trace configuration must specify a valid trace type (call, prestate, or custom), and the target transaction or block must exist in the local chain.
The trace lifecycle must begin with trace initialization before any opcode-level tracing occurs. The tracer must be fully configured with hooks before EVM execution starts.
After trace completion, the trace result must contain all captured opcode executions in order, with accurate gas costs, stack snapshots, and memory changes for each step.
After an error during tracing (e.g., target not found, insufficient resources), the trace must return a well-formed error response and must not leave the node in an inconsistent state.
Tracing must not affect the EVM execution result. The traced execution must produce identical state changes, return values, and gas usage as non-traced execution.
Trace output validation must ensure all captured values are within their expected ranges: gas values are non-negative, program counters are within code bounds, and stack depth does not exceed 1024.
Trace hooks must be called in strict execution order: OnOpcode before OnFault, OnEnter before OnExit for nested calls. Misordered hooks indicate a tracer implementation bug.
After tracing a CALL/CREATE, the trace must include both the parent and child frame traces. The child's OnExit must be recorded before the parent's next opcode.
Error handling during trace must not leak internal node state (memory addresses, file paths, internal error codes) to the RPC caller. Error messages must be sanitized.
A packet received from the UDP network must be at least the minimum packet size and must have a valid tag derived from the recipient's node ID. Packets failing this check must be silently dropped.
Before processing a NODES response from a remote node, the local node must have an outstanding FindNode request to that node. Unsolicited NODES responses must be discarded.

Before establishing a session, the handshake must complete: the initiator sends WHOAREYOU after receiving an unknown packet, and the responder must reply with a valid handshake message containing an ID signature.
After a successful session handshake, both parties must derive identical session keys (encryption key, decryption key, MAC key) from the ECDH shared secret and nonces exchanged.
After receiving valid NODES responses, the node lookup algorithm must update its k-closest set and issue further FindNode requests to newly discovered nodes that are closer to the target.
All Discovery v5 ordinary messages (after session establishment) must be encrypted with AES-128-GCM using the session key. Plaintext ordinary messages must never be processed.
The WHOAREYOU challenge nonce must be unique per handshake attempt. Reuse of a nonce enables replay attacks on the session establishment.
Node records (ENRs) received in NODES responses must have valid signatures and a sequence number greater than or equal to any previously known record for that node ID.
After a node lookup completes (all alpha concurrent queries resolved or timed out), the result must contain the k closest nodes to the target ID found during the lookup.
The ID signature in a handshake message must be verified against the sender's claimed public key. A failed signature verification must abort the handshake and discard the session.

A NODES response must contain no more than the maximum allowed ENR records per message. The total number of ENRs across multiple NODES responses for a single request must not exceed the declared total.
Sessions must expire after a configurable timeout. Expired sessions must require a new handshake before any encrypted communication can resume.
Before processing any packet content, the packet header's protocol version and flag field must be validated. Unknown protocol versions or invalid flags must cause the packet to be dropped.
The Kademlia-based routing table must maintain at most k nodes per distance bucket. When a bucket is full, new nodes replace the least recently seen node only if it fails a liveness check.
Before EVM execution begins, the execution environment (caller, value, gas, input data, code) must be fully initialized from the message call or creation parameters.
After a JUMPI with a zero condition value, the program counter must advance to the next instruction (PC + 1) without jumping. The destination value on the stack is consumed but ignored.
Static call contexts (STATICCALL) must not execute state-modifying opcodes (SSTORE, LOG*, CREATE*, SELFDESTRUCT). Attempting to do so must revert immediately.
Gas metering is monotonically decreasing within a call frame: every opcode execution reduces available gas by at least 1 (the base cost). Gas can only increase via a CALL that returns unused gas.
After a governance vote concludes without meeting quorum, the proposal must remain in pending state and no rule activation occurs.
Rule IDs are globally unique and immutable once assigned. No two governance proposals may share the same rule ID, even across different governance epochs.
Before any opcode restriction check in EOF mode, the execution context must know whether the current code is EOF or legacy. Opcode availability depends entirely on this classification.
EOF containers cannot contain unreachable code sections. Every code section must be reachable from code section 0 via CALLF/JUMPF. Unreachable sections must cause validation failure.
After the fork transition epoch, all gossip topics related to sync committees must use the Altair fork digest. Pre-Altair fork digest messages on these topics must be rejected.
The sync committee period is EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD epochs long. The committee is rotated at the start of each period and remains fixed throughout.
After KECCAK256 execution with an out-of-gas condition, no hash result is produced, the transaction reverts, and all gas in the current call frame is consumed.
KECCAK256 is collision-resistant: no two distinct inputs should produce the same 32-byte output. The EVM's security model (contract addresses, storage keys, ABI encoding) depends on this property.
After including attestations in a block, the block's attestation list must be sorted by committee_index for deterministic SSZ serialization.

Before displaying chain information to the user for approval, the wallet must sanitize all string fields (chainName, nativeCurrency.name, nativeCurrency.symbol) to prevent XSS or UI injection attacks.
After tracing a transaction that reverts, the trace must capture all opcodes executed before the revert, including the REVERT opcode itself and its return data.
The trace output size must be bounded. Implementations should enforce a maximum trace size to prevent memory exhaustion when tracing complex transactions.
After a failed RPC verification (endpoint unreachable or returns wrong chainId), the wallet must inform the user of the failure reason and must not add the chain.
After JUMPF to a function with 0 outputs (non-returning), the return stack entry for the current function is consumed. The callee function must terminate via STOP, RETURN, or REVERT.
After IL validation rejects a submission (invalid committee membership, invalid parent hash, duplicate), the IL is discarded and the submitter receives a rejection notification.
The BLS signature on a sync committee message must be verified against the validator's public key from the beacon state before the message is accepted into the local aggregate.

After receiving a WHOAREYOU challenge, the node must respond with a handshake packet containing a fresh ephemeral public key and ID signature within a reasonable timeout, or the session attempt is abandoned.
KECCAK256 execution must not modify any EVM state (storage, balance, nonce). It is a pure computational operation that only reads memory and writes to the stack.
Each chainId in the wallet's chain registry must be unique. Adding a chain with an existing chainId must not create a duplicate entry but instead update or switch.
The attestation signature must be verified against the expected signing root derived from the AttestationData (without committee_index under EIP-7549) and the validator's public key.
After successful CREATE/CREATE2 execution, the new contract address is deterministically computed and the contract code is stored at that address. The nonce of the creator is incremented.
An EOF container version 1 must have exactly one type section, at least one code section, and at most one data section. Zero code sections or multiple type sections are invalid.
FindNode requests must specify a list of distances (0-256) to query. The responding node must only return ENRs at the requested distances from its own node ID.
A sync committee contribution's aggregation_bits length must exactly equal the number of validators in the corresponding subcommittee. Length mismatches must cause rejection.

Inclusion list transactions must be individually valid (correct nonce, sufficient balance, valid signature) at the time of IL creation. Stale transactions degrade IL utility but do not invalidate the IL itself.
Memory read for KECCAK256 must not access memory beyond the current allocation without paying the expansion cost. The offset + size range defines the minimum required memory size.
The rpcUrls array must contain at least one valid URL. An empty array must be rejected with an invalid params error.
Custom JavaScript tracers (if supported) must be sandboxed with memory and execution time limits. A tracer must not be able to access node internals or the filesystem.
The EVM execution is deterministic: given identical initial state, transaction, and block context, every compliant implementation must produce identical state root, logs, and return data.
After RETURNCONTRACT execution in init mode, the deployed container must include the data section appended from the auxiliary data. The final container must pass EOF validation.
After processing a valid gossip message, the node must rebroadcast it to connected peers according to the gossip protocol parameters (D_out minimum outbound degree).
Rate limiting must be enforced on incoming packets per source IP. Excessive packet rates from a single source must trigger packet dropping to prevent resource exhaustion.
The signing root for attestation signatures under EIP-7549 is computed from AttestationData which no longer contains committee_index. All validators must agree on this new signing root computation.
The wallet must not automatically switch chains or expose user addresses to the dApp until the user explicitly approves. The approval flow is mandatory even for well-known chains.
